scope: Targeted primary design passages; no novelty proof by search absence and no complete evaluation review claimed.

sources.title: Cache Index-Aware Memory Allocation
sources.read_scope: Author PDF pp1-4, introduction, modern allocators, CIF spacing/coloring design; browser lines12-244 and323-353.
sources.covers: Allocator impact on TLB/cache locality, LIFO page-local free lists and cache-index-oriented spacing/coloring are old. Do not claim locality-aware allocation as new.
sources.specific_difference: The reviewed design chooses spacing/cache indices rather than selecting from live resident IOTLB output pages after a real source READ and a concurrent consumer release. This limited observation does not establish first publication of L-F.

sources.title: Providing Task Isolation via TLB Coloring
sources.read_scope: Original author PDF related work and III design, pp2-4, browser lines139-227 and275-373; author project page independently lists DOI.
sources.covers: Controlling virtual allocation to isolate set-associative TLBs, per-color free lists and capacity constraints; prior locking/partitioning is also explicitly discussed.
sources.specific_difference: Native shared IOTLB is fully associative with explicit way masks, so simple set coloring does not directly map to its index. It remains a relevant allocator/locking control; no proof that the whole allocation field omits late selection.

sources.title: Elastic Translations: Fast Virtual Memory with Multiple Translation Sizes
sources.read_scope: Author PDF IV-A, IV-B and IV-D, pp5-7, browser lines679-810 and897-934. Full19-page copy obtained; evaluation not reviewed in full.
sources.covers: Contiguity-aware fault-time allocation, transparent intermediate-size translations, asynchronous promotion and TLB-miss-guided selection. Cannot call matching allocations to translation geometry or hardware feedback broadly new.
sources.specific_difference: The reviewed mechanisms change translation size/layout over page faults and promotion, rather than commit an output-pool parent and choose a free page after a particular actual source operation. Same-cost layout/hugepage/coalescing controls can still eliminate L-F's useful region.

sources.title: Latency reduction for direct memory access operations involving address translation
sources.read_scope: Primary indexed disclosure retrieved by targeted searches: receive descriptor prefetcher and transmit descriptor/buffer prefetcher; full web open failed. Not full patent/claim/legal review.
sources.covers: Ahead-of-demand DMA access to warm descriptor/buffer translations, including dummy reads/writes; therefore translation prefetch and descriptor-triggered preparation are existing approaches.
sources.specific_difference: L-F executes the necessary real source data READ and delays choosing its output, not an additional dummy operation solely to warm the IOTLB. A source-prefetch control must still be allowed an efficient legal implementation; the observed distinction alone proves no independent benefit.

inherited_round02: io_uring provided buffers, DAMN, IOTLB wall, CoLT, AXI-REALM and MASK scopes retain the accepted round02 review. Not re-read or presented as newly fully checked.
still_open: Whether same-contract ordinary source preparation has equal/lower full cost
conditional_verdict: Because existing work covers pooled selection, locality, coloring, translation-size-aware allocation and prefetched translations, none of those individual actions is an independent contribution. If the paid normal-read/late-output-binding integration has a reachable useful full-cost frontier absent from the exact nearest mechanism, it can provide an independent architecture contribution.
